items.claim: The rejected alternative for splitting off web:Isa.51.21-Isa.51.23 does not engage the strongest rival: a repeated cup-of-wrath catchword tying it back to the preceding description.
items.evidence: web:Isa.51.22 says “Your Lord Yahweh, your God who pleads the cause of his people, says, “Behold, I have taken out of your hand the cup of staggering, even the bowl of the cup of my wrath. You will not drink it any more.” (tier: byte), reusing the same cup-of-wrath vocabulary that opens the preceding description at web:Isa.51.17, “Awake, awake! Stand up, Jerusalem, you who have drunk from Yahweh’s hand the cup of his wrath. You have drunken the bowl of the cup of staggering, and drained it.” (tier: byte) -- a byte-provable catchword tie the strongest_rejected_alternative never names. It rejects merger with web:Isa.51.17-Isa.51.20 only on the weaker ground that a fresh imperative opens web:Isa.51.21, without addressing whether the shared cup vocabulary argues the whole span as one lament-and-reversal oracle rather than two.

items.claim: The row twice claims an exact byte match between the doubled imperative at web:Isa.52.1 and the one at web:Isa.51.9, but the two forms differ at the byte tier.
items.evidence: The doubled imperative opening web:Isa.52.1, “Awake, awake! Put on your strength, Zion. Put on your beautiful garments, Jerusalem, the holy city, for from now on the uncircumcised and the unclean will no more come into you.” (tier: byte), and the doubled imperative opening web:Isa.51.9, “Awake, awake, put on strength, arm of Yahweh! Awake, as in the days of old, the generations of ancient times. Isn’t it you who cut Rahab in pieces, who pierced the monster?” (tier: byte), share the same consonants and vowel points but carry different cantillation marks on both words at the pointed-byte level, so the two forms match only at a lower, accent-stripped tier -- not the byte tier the rationale and device_notes both claim ('byte-matching that earlier shape' / 'matching the byte shape... exactly').

items.claim: The one-verse span at web:Isa.52.3 is bounded by its own fresh messenger formula and closes cleanly before a differently-worded formula reopens the next unit.
items.evidence: web:Isa.52.3, “For Yahweh says, “You were sold for nothing; and you will be redeemed without money.”” (tier: byte), is distinct in wording and referent focus from both the imperative closing at web:Isa.52.2, “Shake yourself from the dust! Arise, sit up, Jerusalem! Release yourself from the bonds of your neck, captive daughter of Zion!” (tier: byte), and the separately-worded formula opening web:Isa.52.4, “For the Lord Yahweh says:” (tier: byte); the preceding SAMEKH mark at oshb:Isa.52.2 (tier-3, single-witness) is accurately disclosed, no parashah mark falls inside the span itself, and the frame is correctly identified as divine rather than royal-messenger.

items.claim: The span web:Isa.52.4-Isa.52.6 correctly groups one fresh messenger-formula onset with its internal postpositive signatures rather than fragmenting at each recurrence.
items.evidence: The “For the Lord Yahweh says:” formula opens at oshb:Isa.52.4 (tier: byte); the twice-repeated postpositive 'says Yahweh' within oshb:Isa.52.5 (tier: byte) is correctly held as an internal signature rather than a fresh frame onset, and the double ketiv/qere note at that verse is disclosed accurately as a double note rather than conflated with a single one; the span closes on “Therefore my people shall know my name. Therefore they shall know in that day that I am he who speaks. Behold, it is I.”” (tier: byte) immediately before the unrelated exclamatory address opening web:Isa.52.7.

items.claim: The span web:Isa.52.7-Isa.52.10 is correctly bounded between the self-identification formula that closes the preceding unit and the differently-addressed imperative that opens the next one.
items.evidence: The exclamatory herald description opening web:Isa.52.7, “How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace, who brings good news, who proclaims salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!”” (tier: byte), shares no formulaic or catchword link back to the self-identification formula closing web:Isa.52.6, and the span's own close, “Yahweh has made his holy arm bare in the eyes of all the nations. All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.” (tier: byte, web:Isa.52.10), precedes a fresh doubled imperative addressed to a different party at web:Isa.52.11, “Depart! Depart! Go out from there! Touch no unclean thing! Go out from among her! Cleanse yourselves, you who carry Yahweh’s vessels.” (tier: byte), rather than continuing the watchmen's proclamation; the closing SAMEKH mark at oshb:Isa.52.10 (single-witness) is accurately disclosed and no span-relevant mark inside web:Isa.52.7-Isa.52.9 is omitted.

items.claim: The row's own boundary_rationale misstates its ordinary row-internal seam at web:Isa.52.12 as a frame boundary fixed at the parent-collection line, and its rejected alternative argues from assignment range rather than content.
items.evidence: Nothing marks web:Isa.52.12/web:Isa.52.13 as a parent-collection frame edge: the governing frame for this span runs Isa.49.1-Isa.55.13, so this seam sits well inside it, not at its boundary. Calling the row's own span-end 'the frame boundary this campaign has fixed at the parent-collection line' overstates an ordinary internal oracle seam as a structural frame edge, and the strongest_rejected_alternative argues from the row's own assigned range rather than from content -- even though the doubled imperative opening web:Isa.52.11, “Depart! Depart! Go out from there! Touch no unclean thing! Go out from among her! Cleanse yourselves, you who carry Yahweh’s vessels.” (tier: byte), and the servant material beginning after web:Isa.52.12 do supply a legitimate content-based seam that could have been cited instead.

items.claim: The span web:Isa.52.13-Isa.52.15 is bounded by a genuine first-person divine-voice onset and closes on an argued person-shift, without deciding the servant's referent.
items.evidence: The first-person-possessive 'my servant' onset at web:Isa.52.13, “Behold, my servant will deal wisely. He will be exalted and lifted up, and will be very high.” (tier: byte), belongs to the book's own catalogued divine-voice servant vocabulary, corroborated -- not driven -- by the preceding tier-3 single-witness SAMEKH mark at oshb:Isa.52.12; the span closes before the shift from third-person royal reaction to a first-person-plural report voice at web:Isa.53.1, “Who has believed our message? To whom has Yahweh’s arm been revealed?” (tier: byte), a content-argued addressee/speaker shift rather than an unmarked theme-split. The strongest_rejected_alternative honestly names the live rival (one undivided song through web:Isa.53.12) and the referent of 'my servant' is explicitly left undecided, consistent with the confidence held at medium rather than high in this hazard zone.
